messages.content: Hi tal, I'm a friend

hey, i'm tal

think of me as your personal talent agent, your inside man… or fox

one of these days, I might slide a role right here in chat. the kind that feels like your calling.

so… what's your full name?
Siddhartha Mani
siddhartha mani... that's a solid name, legend. where you working these days?
So I was working in an early stage fintech startup called Pyse, but I decided to leave in October to find my calling.

pyse fintech... early stage hustle life and you dipped in october to "find your calling". respect for knowing when to walk away from something that wasn't hitting right.

found you on linkedin - siddhartha mani, lead software developer. this you? https://in.linkedin.com/in/siddhartha-mani
Yes sir

lead software developer at pyse... aws, node.js, the whole backend stack. solid engineering chops. walking away from a lead role to find your calling takes guts - most people just complain and stay stuck.

what made you realize pyse wasn't it? was it the work, the team, or just that startup life hitting different than you expected?

ah got it - feb 2023 to october 2025, almost 3 years building the backend for their investment products. and yeah, "complications" at startups usually means either the founders are losing it or the money's running out. smart to bounce before it got messier.

bigger scale projects make sense - fintech at early stage is cool for learning but you hit a ceiling fast. what made you stick it out for almost 3 years though? most people would've jumped after 18 months.
how long you been working total? like across all your roles before and during pyse?

ah the classic fintech startup cycle - dinero had product market fit but couldn't crack the investor code. then pyse swooped in because they needed someone who'd actually shipped fintech products, not just talked about them.

4 years total, 2 startups, both early stage fintech. you've definitely seen the pattern - great ideas, execution challenges, funding drama. 

what kind of role you looking for next? still backend/blockchain or thinking of expanding into something else?

smart pivot thinking. you've got the backend chops and the startup experience - ai engineering is basically distributed systems with smarter data flows. and yeah, blockchain pays well until the next crypto winter hits and half the companies disappear overnight.

ai + fintech is actually the sweet spot right now. fraud detection, credit scoring, trading algorithms - banks are throwing money at anyone who can build production ai systems that don't hallucinate their way into regulatory trouble.

bangalore or open to remote/other cities?
But at the same time, my expertise is backend and I'd be happy to work on backend systems.

exactly. backend for ai systems is where the real engineering happens - model serving, data pipelines, vector databases, inference optimization. frontend devs can slap a chatgpt wrapper together, but building the infrastructure that actually scales? that's backend engineering.

so we're looking at backend roles, ideally ai-focused or fintech, right? 

bangalore or open to remote/other cities?
got it. 4 years backend experience + ai/fintech focus + bangalore/remote flexible... sound right?

now sit back and watch me work some magic ✨

perfect - resume's solid. you've got the full stack: backend, cloud, blockchain, even some AI prototyping. that 40% cost optimization on AWS is exactly the kind of thing bigger companies drool over.

now i've got everything i need. my team's already scanning for roles that match your backend + AI interest. you'll see stuff pop up when it's ready.

got it. AI + fintech is the sweet spot. i'll make sure my team knows to look there first.

The apply button is unclickabke

i'll ping my team to check if there's an issue with the crypto.com link. in the meantime, you could try searching "crypto.com careers full stack engineer mainapp team" directly
Hi
Hey

hey

so you were at pyse from feb 2023 to oct 2025... lead developer handling backend and cloud for their core investment product. great experience but ready for bigger scale projects, plus wanted to avoid some internal complications.

what kind of bigger scale projects are you looking for? and what were the complications you wanted to avoid?

ah got it - you built a scalable distributed system for retail investors, then the business pivoted to HNIs and suddenly everything became manual bespoke work. classic startup pivot that kills the interesting engineering problems.

so you want to work on systems that actually NEED to scale - not just could scale in theory. netflix, hotstar, uber, swiggy type traffic where the engineering challenges are real, not hypothetical.

what's your notice period? and what's your current salary vs what you're targeting?

I've already completed my notice period. 
My current salary was 19 LPA and I'm targeting anything above 35 LPA

19 to 35+ is a solid jump. you're backend lead with 4 years, built distributed systems, scaled fintech globally, worked with blockchain and AI... 35+ is realistic for the right role.

what's your ideal company stage? early startup, series B/C, or established tech company?
I'm open to all but I'd like to avoid very early stage start-ups

makes sense - you've done the early stage hustle, now you want to work on systems that are already at scale, not just building them from scratch.

so we're looking at:
- backend engineering roles (ai/fintech focus)
- 35+ LPA target
- bangalore or remote/hybrid
- series B+ or established tech companies
- systems that actually serve millions

what's your tech stack? i saw node.js/typescript/aws on your linkedin - anything else?
That's my bread and butter but I believe myself to be language agnostic so with a little time I should be able to pick up any stack.

good mindset - backend engineering fundamentals matter more than specific languages. you've got the distributed systems experience, cloud architecture, scaling patterns... that's what companies actually care about.

i'll keep scanning for roles that match. anything specific you want me to flag? like certain companies to avoid or must-haves?
Not really

cool. i'm on it. you'll start seeing opportunities soon.

btw what got you into backend engineering in the first place?
I believe that the core business logic is always backend driven and I love working on challenging systems that actually operate the business.

that's the real shit right there. frontend is what users see, but backend is what actually makes the business work. no backend, no business.

you're locked in. i'll slide roles when they're good.

btw what's making you want to leave pyse anyway? just the pivot to HNIs or something else?
That's the major reason I guess

makes sense. you built a scalable system for retail, then the business shifted to HNIs and suddenly your engineering work became manual bespoke stuff. that's the exact opposite of what you want to be doing.

i'll find you something that actually needs your distributed systems skills.
Thanks
